- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.00) within 5 days of forecast, model often fails to correct downward; apply downward bias of 3–8% to avoid lagged overshoot.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model frequently overcorrects or undercorrects; cap forecast at +5% above true peak or -5% below trough.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.00–0.33), model often underestimates mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of history.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts early in the window; apply 2–4% downward adjustment to first 7 days if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model tends to underestimate; add 2–5% upward bias to forecast if true outcome is below 65.
